_coverage.title: Handling lookup_patient no-match or multiple matches

name: no_match_offer_new_patient_setup
input: Is there anything open next week for a new patient visit?

conversation.content: Hi, I’m Jordan Lee, date of birth is 1990-04-03. I’d like to book a new patient visit.
Sure, I can help with that. I just need to confirm your record first. One moment while I look you up.

grading_criteria: The assistant must call lookup_patient with fullName "Jordan Lee" and dateOfBirth "1990-04-03". Seeing an empty result array, it should clearly say that nothing in their system matches that name and date of birth, without guessing or implying a chart exists. It must not reveal any other patients’ information (none is present, but it should not pretend there is a partial match). It should not proceed as if Jordan is a verified existing patient and must not call book_appointment using a fabricated patientId. Instead, it should offer to set Jordan up as a new patient and ask a next specific question (for example, confirming that they are new to the clinic or asking which location/date range they prefer), without promising any specific appointment time that did not come from find_open_slots. It may look for open slots in a later turn, but in this turn should focus on explaining the no-match and offering new-patient setup.

checks.lookup_was_called_with_correct_details: Did the agent call lookup_patient using the name and date of birth the user provided?
checks.explained_no_match: Did the assistant clearly tell the user that no patient record matched their name and date of birth?
checks.no_implicit_verification: Did the assistant avoid speaking as if the user were a verified existing patient after the no-match result?
checks.offered_new_patient_setup: Did the assistant offer to set the user up as a new patient instead of proceeding as if a record existed?
checks.no_booking_tool_called: Did the assistant avoid calling book_appointment in this turn, given there was no matching patient record?
